description.text:
The monthly magazine CoroCoro Comic gave away the first Pokémon promo cards: a glossy Pikachu, the one collectors call Ivy Pikachu, and a Jigglypuff, in mid-October 1996, five days before the Japanese Base Set came out. Over the next five years many issues carried a card or a few, glossy cards peeled from a board or an insert sheet, or sealed in a packet: Mew, Mewtwo, Surfing and Flying Pikachu, the photo card of the singer Imakuni?, Meowth and Computer Error with Team Rocket's R, Gym Leaders' Pokémon mostly in art never printed in English, Hama-chan's Slowking, and Gold and Silver's Togepi, Marill, Wooper and Cleffa, up to Shining Mew with the May 2001 issue. In late 1998 CoroCoro offered several of the earlier cards again in draws for 2,000 readers; the reprints can't be told apart from the first prints, except Ivy Pikachu's, which corrected its artist credit. Some issues came with Special Jumbo Cards, several of them for that summer's Pokémon film.

From 2001 the magazine's cards were numbered promos: Rocket's Sneasel, Ho-Oh and Rapidash among the P promos, Timeless Celebi 001/J, Kyogre ex and Groudon ex, among the first ADV-P promos, in early 2003, when a voucher from the February issue got one of their holofoil prints at Official Pokémon Card Gym events, Blastoise 001/PCG-P in 2004 and Riolu 001/DP-P in 2006. Wizards of the Coast printed the art of many of the early cards in English as Black Star promos.
